items.title: The sign in the boundary of a cup product of Cech cohomology classes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter cohomology.tex (Cohomology of Sheaves)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of a short exact sequence of complexes of sheaves with a compatible product, the lemma computes the boundary of a cup product: for a in H^n(X, F_3) and b in H^m(X, G_1) one has gamma_1(boundary(a) cup b) = (-1)^{n+1} gamma_3(a cup boundary(b)) (statement lines 5656-5669). The proof is a concrete cocycle computation: after fixing the notation that identifies F_1 as a subsheaf of F_2 with quotient F_3 and G_3 as a subsheaf of G_2 with quotient G_1 (proof lines 5672-5686), the author picks cocycles alpha_3 and beta_1 on a covering, lifts them to cochains alpha_2 and beta_2, observes that alpha_1 = d(alpha_2) and beta_3 = d(beta_2) represent the two boundary classes (proof lines 5689-5715), and then evaluates d(gamma_2(alpha_2 cup beta_2)) through a four-term chain that uses the Leibniz rule for the total complex and the compatibility of the products gamma_i with the boundary maps (proof lines 5716-5730). The claim is H2: nothing is left to the reader, but the content is bookkeeping of degrees and signs inside the total complex, and the final sign is remarked to depend on the sign conventions for the long exact sequence recorded in the author's footnote.
